paper.title: Optimal Allocation Strategies for the Dark Pool Problem

settings.name_in_paper: Dark pool problem with fractional (continuous-valued) allocations
unmapped: Allocate volume V^t <= V among K venues; reward at venue i is min(v_i, s_i) (censored feedback: only the consumed amount per venue observed)
Learner knows the volume bound V
Comparator: best fixed assignment of each unit v in {1..V} to a venue
Reward is concave piecewise linear in allocations
settings.definition_quote: A learning algorithm receives a sequence of volumes V^1,...,V^T where V^t in {1,...,V}. It has K available venues, amongst which it can allocate up to V^t units at time t. ... The learner then receives the number of units r_i^t = min(v_i^t, s_i^t) consumed at venue i. We allow the sequence of volumes and maximum consumption levels to be chosen adversarially

settings.name_in_paper: Dark pool problem with integral allocations, oblivious adversary
unmapped: Integer allocations of V^t <= V units among K venues; reward min(u_i, s_i) per venue with censored feedback
Learner knows the volume bound V
Comparator: best fixed assignment of units to venues
settings.definition_quote: In this section we describe a low regret algorithm that allocates an integral number of units to each venue. ... An oblivious adversary is one that chooses V^t and s_i^t without seeing the algorithm's (random) allocations u_i^t.

settings.name_in_paper: Dark pool problem with integral allocations, adaptive adversary
unmapped: Integer allocations of V^t <= V units among K venues; censored feedback
Learner knows the volume bound V
settings.definition_quote: We allow the sequence of volumes and maximum consumption levels to be chosen adversarially, i.e. V_t, s_i^t can depend on {v_i^1,...,v_i^{t-1}}

settings.name_in_paper: Dark pool problem with integral allocations (lower bound)
unmapped: Integer allocations of V units among K venues with V_t = V fixed; liquidities s_i^t in {0, V} iid
Lower bound combines a stochastic construction (sqrt(TVK)) with the experts reduction (V sqrt(T ln K)), the latter an adversarial construction
settings.definition_quote: As before we consider a special case with V_t = V at every round. Following Auer et al., we construct K different distributions for generating the liquidities s_i^t. At each round, the i_th distribution samples s_i^t = V with probability (1/2 + eps) and s_j^t = V with probability 1/2 for j != i.

algorithms.name: Exponentiated gradient algorithm for continuous-valued allocations (ExpGrad, Algorithm 1)
Algorithm 2 with variance-corrected gradient estimator g-hat

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on per-round volumes V^t

source.label: thm:regretfrac
source.quote: For any choices of the volumes $\vol{t}\in[0,V]$ and of the maximum consumption levels $\limit{i}{t}$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:fracalloc} with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{(e-2)T}}$ over $T$ rounds is $O(V\sqrt{T\ln K})$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit 3 V sqrt(T ln K). Deterministic algorithm, so bound holds for every sequence. Section 3.2 argues (informally, not as a numbered statement) a matching Omega(V sqrt(T ln K)) lower bound via reduction from experts.

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on per-round volumes V^t

source.label: thm:regretintexp
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg:intallocexp}, with $\eta = \left(\frac{V(\ln K)^2}{KT^2}\right)^{1/3}$, has expected regret over $T$ rounds of $O((VTK)^{2/3}(\ln K)^{1/3})$, where $V$ is the bound on volumes $\vol{t}$, and the volumes and maximum consumption levels $\limit{i}{t}$ are chosen by an oblivious adversary.

results.notes: Proof ends with 6(VTK)^{2/3}(ln K)^{1/3}. Sampling distribution over subsets exists (Theorem 2) but efficient construction deferred to full version, so compute not stated.

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on per-round volumes V^t

source.label: thm:regretintprob
source.quote: With probability at least 1 - $\frac{1}{T}$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:intallocexp} using the gradient estimator $\gh_t$ against oblivious adversaries is $\widetilde{O}\left(V(TK)^{2/3}\right)$.

symbols.V_vol: upper bound on per-round volumes V^t

source.quote: With probability at least 1 - $\frac{1}{T}$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:intallocexp} against adaptive adversaries is $\widetilde{O}\left(V^2(TK)^{2/3}\right)$.

results.notes: Obtained via union bound over K^V comparators; algorithm presumably the variance-corrected version. Paper also notes an online-to-batch iid consequence of Õ(V^2 T^{-1/3} K^{2/3}) per-round suboptimality (not recorded).

symbols.V_vol: volume per round (V_t = V in the construction)

source.label: thm:regretlbexp
source.quote: Any algorithm that plays integer valued allocations has expected regret that is $\Omega\left(\sqrt{TV(K+V\ln K)}\right).$

results.notes: Combines sqrt(TVK) from a stochastic Auer-et-al. construction with V sqrt(T ln K) from an adversarial experts reduction; setting recorded as stochastic for the first part.
